claims.text: Pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle-size distribution typical of metallic additive manufacturing is a suitable initial feedstock.
High-entropy alloys can be fabricated by LPBF or selective laser melting from powder feedstocks.
The build platform, and optionally the surrounding powder bed, should be preheated throughout LPBF deposition.
Approximately 300–500 °C is an applicable preheating window for LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi.
Platform or powder-bed preheating reduces the thermal gradient along the build direction.
A reduced thermal gradient moderates cooling rates during layerwise processing.
A reduced thermal gradient diminishes thermal-contraction differences between successive layers.
Moderated cooling and contraction differences reduce residual-stress accumulation.
Reducing the temperature gradient decreases microstructural defects associated with rapid solidification.
Preheating promotes a more homogeneous microstructure in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi builds will have statistically significantly lower residual stress than room-temperature LPBF builds.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi builds will have higher microhardness than room-temperature LPBF builds.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi builds will have improved tensile performance relative to room-temperature LPBF builds.
Conventional room-temperature LPBF commonly produces high residual stresses because of rapid thermal cycling.
Conventional room-temperature LPBF degrades the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
An inert processing atmosphere limits oxidation during LPBF of the feedstock.
The effectiveness of preheating may be confined to miniature components because their low thermal mass permits more uniform preheating.
Applying the intervention to larger components or other alloy compositions may require additional parameter optimization.
